title: Officer who fired fatal shot feared for his life
article: A junior Vancouver police officer who shot a man who was stabbing his partner testified yesterday that he fired because he thought the man would kill them both.

"I feared for my life and for the life of my partner," Const. John Filipelli, at the time a three-year veteran of the force, told the inquest into the shooting death of Dean Nicholas Andrusyk, 49, on Sept. 28, 2004.
The two officers were responding to a call from a male who said he was engaged in a domestic dispute. He asked them to meet him at the 7-Eleven store near East 41st Avenue and Victoria Drive.
The officers drove up without lights or sirens.
Andrusyk, who wasn't the complainant, was sitting on a park bench not far from the store. He gestured at the cruiser twice as if holding and shooting a rifle.
He then aggressively approached the cruiser's passenger door, where Const. Craig Look was sitting, and refused to move.
Look, who had graduated from the police academy six months earlier, kicked open the door from the inside and got out, yelling at Andrusyk to "get back, get back."
The two struggled "chest to chest," with Look "trapped" against the door by Andrusyk.
Andrusyk then started stabbing at Look's chest with a serrated knife.
Look, who was wearing a Kevlar vest reinforced by a metal "trauma plate" over the sternum, said it felt like he was being punched twice in the chest.
The third strike slashed him "to the bone" in the arm. He also suffered a number of other smaller cuts.
"I yelled to John, 'I'm getting stabbed,' " said Look.
Filipelli repeatedly demanded that Andrusyk drop his knife. When Andrusyk turned toward him, still holding the knife, Filipelli shot him in the chest.
The officers estimated the incident took 15 to 30 seconds. They called for backup and an ambulance, and handcuffed and searched Andrusyk for more weapons.

Ambulance attendant Patrick Seline told the inquest he and his partner were responding to a call for a stabbed officer and it wasn't until they arrived that Seline "noticed a gentleman lying on his back about 20 \[metres\] away."
Seline walked over and when he noticed blood on the man's shirt, the officer standing nearby said, "We shot him."

Seline ripped off the still-conscious Andrusyk's T-shirt, sent the officer for oxygen and got Andrusyk into another ambulance. Emergency staff at Vancouver General Hospital tried to save his life, but Andrusyk died in hospital at 2 a.m., two hours after the shooting.

The inquest heard that Andrusyk suffered from schizophrenia. Toxicology tests found no drugs, prescription or otherwise, or alcohol in his system. But pathologist Dr. Charles Lee noted tests were done after he had been given fluids and his blood likely was diluted.
A police investigation of the incident found the officers acted in self-defence.
The inquest continues today.
